en: Clouds in the sky are made of tiny liquid water droplets or solid ice crystals, not water vapor.
Philippine seawater is a homogeneous mixture where dissolved salt acts as the solute and water acts as the solvent.
Iron roofs turning reddish-brown during the rainy season undergo a chemical change that creates a new substance called iron oxide.
Melting ice candy on a hot afternoon involves a physical change where solid ice becomes a liquid without forming a new substance.
Pumice stones from volcanic eruptions float on water because their porous structure makes them less dense than the liquid.
The white sand on Boracay Beach contains tiny pieces of quartz, a hard mineral that resists weathering better than softer rocks.
Floodwater after a typhoon is a heterogeneous suspension mixture where solid soil particles are temporarily suspended in liquid water before settling.
Fallen mango leaves decaying in a compost pile undergo a chemical change as microorganisms break them down into nutrient-rich soil humus.
Drying wet school uniforms under the sun causes a physical change where liquid water evaporates into invisible water vapor.
Wooden spatulas are used to stir hot adobo because wood is a poor thermal conductor that prevents heat from burning your hand.
The sweet scent of sampaguita flowers spreads across a garden because volatile gas molecules diffuse rapidly through the surrounding air.
Fresh coconut milk is a colloid, a specific mixture where tiny liquid fat droplets are evenly dispersed throughout liquid water.
